lane: intensity: 1 km new-fault-density zoning + presence-only point-process intensity with target-group background; sparse 3 px lattice above break-even
hypothesis: Unmapped fault density is predictable at 1 km block scale from the same geophysical and topographic evidence that predicts mapped faults, once the mapping process (observer effort) is absorbed by a target-group background; deploying only the evidence terms and re-deriving the block break-even turns that density into a sparse dot field that is not a re-prediction of the catalogue.
mechanism: Presence-only logistic (log) intensity fitted on thinned catalogue pixels vs random background; presence thinning 2 px; 150,000 background points; ridge lambda selected by spatial CV; deployment zeroes the intercept and drops neglog_dist_catalogue / cat_density_1km (EVIDENCE_FAMILY). Block shares -> expected scored-fault pixels per 1 km block -> absolute-density strata (edges 2.5/5/10/20 px) -> spacing table -> lattice sites inside the study-area footprint minus the mapped catalogue.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Map-scale geophysical texture that correlates with structure without being a fault: lithologic and cover contacts, magnetic dike swarms, erosional and range-front lineaments, and flight-line acquisition artefacts; plus the observer process itself -- where the region was mapped well (and at what scale) controls where new faults can be recognised, which the effort covariates only partially absorb.

evidence_holdout_catalogue.note: Catalogue hide-and-recover; withheld pixels are a subset of the mapped catalogue, so this frame can rank emission rules but cannot rank field quality for the real (off-catalogue) target. Not an organizer score.

evidence_independent_frame.frame: SGMC novelty = SGMC faults >3 px from the mapped catalogue (61,664 px); a different public catalogue, NOT organizer truth

literal_leg.note: overlap leg is 1.0 by construction against dense-support priors; reported with an explicit exclusion note, not exempted (IR-59-REPR-01)

correlation_overlap_vs_registry.saturation_note: the literal/representation-aware trip (0.9952 against 13GEMSDOE) is a uniform-lattice saturation artefact: that prior is a regular lattice covering the whole footprint (206,895 dots), within 3 px of almost any candidate dot; only 0.1204 of ITS dots are within 3 px of ours, and the rank correlation is -0.003. See IR-59-REPR-01.

verdict.note: literal-leg overlap against dense-support priors is 1.0 by construction for any nonempty candidate and is reported, not exempted (IR-59-REPR-01).

surface_before_placement.note: shares are relative intensity; the absolute conversion uses a stated design projection (g_total), which is sensitivity-tested, never scored

local_validation.validation_class: local format/range preflight; not organizer acceptance or uniqueness clearance

validator_output.status: locally validated within separately recorded inventory scope; not organizer acceptance or slot approval

submission_note: Zoned 1 km new-fault density, presence-only intensity with mapping-effort background correction; 3 px lattice above break-even.
promotion_requires: owner selector step (protocol item 6); 0 slots used in-session; see verdict_reason for what is still unresolved
verdict_reason: DOWNLOAD OK: format-validated, all-finite, in [0,1], 0 dots on the catalogue; no drift trip on the meaningful tests -- worst rank correlation against all 710 registry rasters is 0.1142 (limit 0.90) and the worst comparable-peer overlap is 0.5129 (limit 0.70, tier = sparse peers at most 2 % of footprint). The literal representation-aware leg reports 0.9952 against a full-footprint uniform lattice, which is a saturation artefact, not shared structure: only 0.1204 of that lattice is within 3 px of our dots (IR-59-REPR-01); canary-clean (worst AUC 0.5299 vs 0.90). SUBMIT HOLD: the evidence of an advantage is mixed and the repository will not spend a competition slot on it. On the off-catalogue frame (the declared arbiter, because the scored target is faults ABSENT from the catalogue) this exact release is 0.04399 [0.03231, 0.05601] vs the proximity control 0.03914 [0.03301, 0.04594], paired difference +0.00485 [-0.00814, +0.01893] -- not significant. On the catalogue hide-and-recover frame it is 0.03339 vs proximity 0.23490 and uniform 0.03468, because that frame mechanically rewards placing dots beside the visible catalogue and the live evidence (OWNER-REPORTED, n=15) penalises exactly that (-0.544 within 2 px of the catalogue, +0.766 median distance to the catalogue). The matched-budget family comparison DID favour a ground-only field on the arbiter frame (0.05708 vs 0.03548 proximity, +61 %) but at a different emission configuration, so it is not a claim about this raster. What would flip the verdict: a release regenerated at that matched-budget configuration and re-scored on the arbiter frame with a lower bound above zero, or the owner's selector step choosing this file against the family's retained candidates.

live_profile.note: the owner-reported live structure (n=15) is: log-dot-count -0.810, dots within 2 px of the catalogue -0.544, median distance to the catalogue +0.766; this profile is reported so the release can be compared with that structure, not because it is a score

limitations: No organizer receipt: every score here is a holdout proxy or owner-reported context.
Catalogue holdout over-rewards dots (withheld catalogue pixels ~30x denser than the estimated new-fault population); the tie-break to the smaller budget is a declared policy, not a correction.
SGMC novelty is a different public catalogue, not the organizer's new faults.
USGS reliability-of-location class cannot be joined to the grid (IR-59-EFFORT-02); no roads dataset was available in any clone.
Feature stack verified by transport hashes, not by an official provenance receipt.
